answer: Sybil resistance starts with a public mesa cairn. I pin a numbered quill to a carved slot, then press a fresh yarrow sprig over a SHA-256(address|epoch|nonce|seed) stamp that faces the south trail. A noon photo must show the quill, the sprig, and the slot number together; the photo hash is posted beside the cairn. Three unaffiliated ridge stewards, none of whom have vouched for me before, each lock 55 POA for ten days. A second identity needs a new quill, a different slot, and a 200 POA lock. A missing stamp, a reused hash, or a photo taken off the noon window cuts the bond 70%.
